name: Magus Tirth
summary: At the Mirage Raceway, Magus Tirth tends chickens, serves drinks, and stakes books on the races. The human wizard lives on the Shimmering Flats, where he torments his apprentice and has wagered away valuable works.

sections.title: A Wizard in the Dust
sections.body:
Magus Tirth makes his home beside the roaring Shimmering Flats. Mages of his skill often study in Dalaran or Stormwind, but he sells chickens and drinks to passersby. He gambles and watches the rocket cars race.

His apprentice, 'Plucky' Johnson, lives under a curse that has turned him into a chicken. Beneath Tirth’s odd habits lies true arcane mastery. He wrote esoteric books on magical power, then lost them in reckless wagers at the speedway.

sections.title: Rituals and Debts
sections.body:
Magus Tirth once owned a manual called 'Rituals of Power', sought by practicing mages. Gambling debts at the Mirage Raceway drove him to sell his own work to an agent of the Scarlet Crusade. The sale settled his losses.

Now apprentices and seekers of knowledge must track the book into hostile territory.

faq.q: Why is Magus Tirth out in the desert?
faq.answer: Magus Tirth lives on the Shimmering Flats beside the Mirage Raceway, drawn by its spectacle and gambling. He watches the gnome and goblin racers, sells chickens, and indulges his vices instead of pursuing a scholarly life in a major city.

faq.q: Who is the chicken next to him?
faq.answer: The chicken beside Magus Tirth is 'Plucky' Johnson, his apprentice. Tirth cursed Johnson into chicken form and can no longer remember why, though he is sure the little ingrate deserved it.

faq.q: What is the book Rituals of Power?
faq.answer: 'Rituals of Power' is an advanced treatise on arcane energy written by Magus Tirth. Mages use it to advance their craft, but Tirth sold his copy to pay his racing debts.

faq.q: Why is his book difficult to obtain?
faq.answer: Magus Tirth no longer has his copy of 'Rituals of Power'. Mages seeking it must follow up on his account of how he parted with the tome.

angles.text: As a mage, you can study Magus Tirth’s treatise 'Rituals of Power' to deepen your understanding of arcane power.
